statement.summary: Theorem 5.1 is frozen as the single Prop `kActiveStatement`: for n ≥ 2, d ≥ 1, σ ≥ 1, k ≤ n^d and every state a : Fin σ, the integer cast of `numKActive n d σ a k` (= |S^a_{n^d,k}|) equals `kActiveRHS n d σ k`. The right-hand side is the sum of `kActiveSummand` over the nonzero rank vectors; the §5 binomial convention (annihilation of the whole summand unless k/h(v) is an integer in {0,…,N/h(v)}) is encoded as an `if … then … else 0` guard inside `kActiveSummand`, and the guard is proved equivalent to the paper's rational condition (`guard_iff`).
deltas: Alphabet Σ is `Fin σ` (only |Σ| = σ enters); the fixed state a is universally quantified after σ (the paper fixes a before the theorem); the right-hand side does not depend on a, as in the paper.
|S^a_{n^d,k}| is `numKActive` = `Nat.card` of the subtype of shift-symmetric configurations with `cellsInState s a = k`; the equation is stated in ℤ (the right-hand side is a signed sum).

Rank vectors are functions `n.primeFactors → ℕ` with values in {0,…,d} (`Fintype.piFinset … Finset.range (d + 1)`): coordinates are labelled by the prime p itself rather than by its index i in p_1 < ⋯ < p_{ω(n)}; v ≠ 0 is `.erase 0`.

r_d(p,v) is `rdCoeff p v d = p^{C(v,2)} · gaussBinom p d v`; `gaussBinom` is the q-Pascal recurrence, linked to the paper's product formula by the separately frozen and proved `ShiftSym.P01.gaussBinomProductFidelityStatement`.

§5 convention: the summand is `if h(v) ∣ k ∧ k/h(v) ≤ N/h(v) then … else 0` with ℕ-division; `guard_iff` proves this guard is exactly 'k/h(v) is an integer in {0,…,N/h(v)}' with rational quotients. Under k ≤ N the second conjunct is automatic once h(v) ∣ k.
N/h(v), k/h(v), (N−k)/h(v) are ℕ-divisions, exact: h(v) ∣ n^d (`hVec_dvd_pow`), h(v) ∣ k by the guard, and n^d − k is untruncated because k ≤ n^d is a hypothesis.
σ − 1 is computed in ℤ (no truncated subtraction); 0^0 = 1 is Lean's `pow_zero` (the paper's convention, relevant only at σ = 1, k = N).

The annihilation rule is applied only to binom(N/h(v), k/h(v)); the binom(v_i,2) inside r_d is the ordinary `Nat.choose` — exactly the v5 paper wording ('all other binomial coefficients are the ordinary ones'). The Lean docstrings still record a PAPER ISSUE about the scope of the convention as worded in v3.1 ('Here and below'); that wording has since been replaced in the paper by the restricted one, so the issue is resolved in v5.

maps.label: |S^a_{n^d,k}| = Σ_{v≠0} (−1)^{1+|v|} ∏ r_d(p_i,v_i) C(N/h, k/h) (σ−1)^{(N−k)/h}

lean.text: (numKActive n d σ a k : ℤ) = kActiveRHS n d σ k

maps.note: Equality in ℤ of the cast count and the frozen right-hand side.

maps.label: n ≥ 2, d ≥ 1, σ ≥ 1, 0 ≤ k ≤ N

tex.text: For all integers $n\ge2$, $d, \sigma\ge1$, and $0\le k\le N=n^d$

maps.note: Same four hypotheses, as antecedents; 0 ≤ k is automatic for k : ℕ.

maps.label: n ≥ 2
maps.note: Makes the lattice finite and nontrivial (Definition 2.1's standing hypothesis).

maps.label: d ≥ 1
maps.note: The paper writes d, σ ≥ 1 together. Kept as in the paper; the proof does not use it (see the proof block).

maps.label: σ ≥ 1 (counting statement)
maps.note: Definition 2.1 allows σ = 1 for counting statements; with σ = 1 the type `Fin σ` is inhabited, so a : Fin σ exists.

maps.label: 0 ≤ k ≤ N = n^d
maps.note: N is written out as n ^ d throughout; k : ℕ gives 0 ≤ k for free. This hypothesis also makes the ℕ-subtraction n ^ d − k in the exponent exact.

maps.label: a fixed state a ∈ Σ, Σ = Fin σ
maps.note: The paper fixes a ∈ Σ in the section preamble; Lean quantifies over every a : Fin σ (equivalent: the theorem holds for each fixed a, and any alphabet of size σ is a relabeling of Fin σ).

maps.label: |S^a_{n^d,k}|

lean.text: (numKActive n d σ a k : ℤ)

maps.note: Natural-number cardinality cast to ℤ.

maps.label: S^a_{n^d,k} = shift-symmetric configurations with exactly k cells in state a

tex.text:
let $S^a_{n^d,k}$ be the set of
shift-symmetric configurations with exactly $k$ cells in state $a$

lean.text: Nat.card {s : Config n d (Fin σ) // IsShiftSymmetric s ∧ cellsInState s a = k}

maps.note: `Nat.card` of the subtype of configurations Lat n d → Fin σ satisfying both conditions; genuine cardinality since the type is finite for n ≥ 1.

maps.label: shift-symmetric: Stab(s) ≠ {0}

lean.text: ∃ v : Lat n d, v ≠ 0 ∧ shift v s = s

maps.note: Definition 2.3: some nonzero translation fixes s (equivalently its stabilizer is nontrivial); `shift v s u = s (u + v)` is τ_v.

maps.label: exactly k cells in state a

lean.text: Nat.card {u : Lat n d // s u = a}

maps.note: #{u ∈ ℤ_n^d : s(u) = a} = k.

maps.label: Σ over v ∈ {0,…,d}^{ω(n)}, v ≠ 0

lean.text: ∑ v ∈ (rankVectors n d).erase 0, kActiveSummand n d σ k v

maps.note: The right-hand side is a finite sum over the nonzero rank vectors of the summand `kActiveSummand`.

maps.label: index set {0,…,d}^{ω(n)} ∖ {0}
maps.note: {0,…,d} = `Finset.range (d + 1)`; the product set over the coordinates is `Fintype.piFinset`; v ≠ 0 removes the zero function (`.erase 0`).

maps.label: one coordinate per distinct prime factor p_1 < ⋯ < p_{ω(n)}

tex.text:
the rank vectors here run over $\vv\in\{0,\dots,d\}^{\omega(n)}$,
with one coordinate per distinct prime factor
the number of distinct prime factors of $n$ is $k=\omega(n)$

maps.note: Coordinates are indexed by the prime p ∈ n.primeFactors itself instead of by its position i in the increasing list; a bijection, and every summand only uses ∏_i and Σ_i, so it is symmetric under relabelling. (The §3 letter k = ω(n) is renamed here because k is the active-cell count.)

maps.label: the summand at v

lean.text:
(-1 : ℤ) ^ (1 + absVec v) * (∏ p : n.primeFactors, (rdCoeff p (v p) d : ℤ))
      * ((n ^ d / hVec v).choose (k / hVec v) : ℤ)
      * ((σ : ℤ) - 1) ^ ((n ^ d - k) / hVec v)

maps.note: The then-branch of `kActiveSummand`: sign × coefficient product × binomial × power, in ℤ, in the paper's order.

maps.label: (−1)^{1+|v|}
maps.note: Integer power of −1.

maps.label: |v| = Σ_i v_i
maps.note: Defined in Theorem 4.4 and reused here; the sum runs over the primes (= coordinates).

maps.label: ∏_{i=1}^{ω(n)} r_d(p_i, v_i)

lean.text: ∏ p : n.primeFactors, (rdCoeff p (v p) d : ℤ)

maps.note: Product over the distinct primes of n; r_d(p_i,v_i) is `rdCoeff p (v p) d` (argument order q, v, d), cast to ℤ.

maps.label: r_d(p,v) = p^{C(v,2)} [d v]_p
maps.note: Same formula; r_d(p,0) = 1 holds since C(0,2) = 0 and gaussBinom q dd 0 = 1.

maps.label: binom(v,2) is the ordinary binomial (not under the §5 convention)

tex.text: all other binomial coefficients are the ordinary ones

maps.note: The binomial inside r_d is `Nat.choose` and never annihilates the summand (C(0,2) = C(1,2) = 0 just gives p^0 = 1), matching the v5 wording that restricts the convention to binom(N/h, k/h).

maps.label: Gaussian binomial [d r]_p

lean.text:
(∏ i ∈ Finset.range r, (((p : ℚ) ^ (d - i) - 1) / ((p : ℚ) ^ (i + 1) - 1))) =
      (gaussBinom p d r : ℚ)

maps.note: Lean defines the Gaussian binomial by the q-Pascal recurrence; agreement with the paper's product formula (for primes p, d ≥ 1, r ≤ d) is a separately frozen and proved fidelity statement of group 01.

maps.label: h(v) = ∏_i p_i^{v_i}
maps.note: Product over the distinct primes of n, in ℕ.

maps.label: C(N/h(v), k/h(v))

lean.text: ((n ^ d / hVec v).choose (k / hVec v) : ℤ)

maps.note: Ordinary `Nat.choose` of two ℕ-quotients, evaluated only in the then-branch of the convention guard (where both quotients are exact), cast to ℤ.

maps.label: N/h(v)
maps.note: ℕ-division, exact because h(v) ∣ n^d for every rank vector (`hVec_dvd_pow`, proved; the paper's 'Integrality' remark in the proof of Theorem 4.4).

maps.label: k/h(v)
maps.note: ℕ-division, exact in the then-branch since the guard contains h(v) ∣ k.

maps.label: (σ−1)^{(N−k)/h(v)}, with 0^0 := 1
maps.note: Monoid power in ℤ with exponent in ℕ; Lean's `pow_zero` gives 0^0 = 1, which is the paper's convention (the claim that it matters only at σ = 1, k = N is frozen separately as `zeroPowRelevanceStatement`).

maps.label: σ − 1 in ℤ
maps.note: Computed in ℤ, so no truncated ℕ-subtraction (it is 0 exactly at σ = 1).

maps.label: (N−k)/h(v)
maps.note: ℕ-subtraction is exact because k ≤ n^d (hypothesis); the ℕ-division is exact in the then-branch because h(v) divides both n^d and k.

maps.label: §5 convention: C(N/h,k/h) := 0 unless k/h ∈ {0,…,N/h} ∩ ℤ, annihilating the whole summand

tex.text:
$\binom{N/h}{k/h}:=0$ whenever
$k/h$ is not an integer in $\{0,\dots,N/h\}$, and such a vanishing
binomial annihilates its
whole summand

lean.text: hVec v ∣ k ∧ k / hVec v ≤ n ^ d / hVec v

maps.note: The whole summand (sign, coefficients, binomial and power) is replaced by 0 when the guard fails, so the fractional exponent is never evaluated. Given h(v) ∣ k and k ≤ N, the second conjunct is automatic; it is kept to mirror 'in {0,…,N/h}'.

maps.label: guard ⇔ 'k/h(v) is an integer in {0,…,N/h(v)}' (rational quotients)
maps.note: Proved infrastructure lemma (not a paper claim) showing that the ℕ-encoded guard says exactly what the paper's convention says, with the quotients read literally in ℚ.
